speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in identifying a site for potential aquaculture activities (a) what are the considerations by the Government; and (b) what are the procedures in place for expert and public consultation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The EIA process involves robust engagement with agencies, stakeholders and nature groups to review the proposed mitigating and monitoring measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: But beyond the EIA process, SFA also regularly engages with the nature groups and the academics as well, to keep them apprised of aquaculture development plans and works closely with them to understand the impacts of sea-based farming on our local marine environment.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In terms of the types of aquaculture activities being planned, does the Ministry have a view as to whether (a) close-looped recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) farms which may have less impact on the surrounding ecosystems are preferred versus (b) an open-cage sea farming, which, on the other hand, may be more energy-intensive, is a better way forward for Singapore?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Second, while it is time-consuming, I do think that consultation is ultimately a trust-building exercise.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But beyond experts, it is also really important to get the public involved and the buy-in from Singaporeans towards the Singapore Food Story and where Singapore food comes from.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, how can the Ministry better educate and consult with the public so that more are aware about Singapore local produce?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The first one is a technical one on what type of sea farming systems, whether it is RAS, which is a closed containment type, or whether the Ministry would also support open-cage farming.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We leave it to the expertise of the various farm operators to decide which platform they are more comfortable with.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But, of course, we do take into consideration the nature of the sensitive receptacles in the region where farming has to take place, as well as the type of water quality, in advising the operators to choose an appropriate platform that can be used to sustain their operations in a way that is sustainable for the business but, importantly, also sustainable for the marine environment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Clearly, there are advantages and disadvantages to each type of farming methodology and the Member has also pointed out that RAS, while it may have less impact on the environment, it is a lot more energy-intensive.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Yet, at the same time, the advantage it affords is that it has a closed containment system that allows better oxygenation of water and a purer water quality, a more controlled environment that also has the advantage of allowing a more dense stocking of the biomass.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think the operator would need to make a business case to decide whether the pros and cons will pan out for them from a business consideration as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The open-cage sea farming method will allow for quite dense stocking if it can have a certain depth of water to support that.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But the hydrology and the nature of the water in which the cage is to be situated will impact the ability of that method of farming to be viable because there will be a larger impact on the environment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On the other hand, I think it does mean that there are possibly less energy requirements using an open-cage method.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, there are different considerations at play here.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: What we try to do is to encourage operators to practise good husbandry so that the fish can be kept safe and in a bio-secure manner.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And at the same time, to ensure that their practice of growing the fish does not foul the water conditions, by using proper sustainable feeding methodology in their farming practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The second question is whether we can engage more with the public to encourage public support for local produce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: At the same time, the Alliance for Action also looks at how we can educate the public to raise consumer awareness of how they can support our local produce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And, not least, to make sure that there is less carbon footprint incurred in our food supplies by sourcing more locally but, importantly, also to build up the appetite for local produce to grow their market here and, in the process, build a more resilient supply chain for ourselves and food security for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think the Senior Minister of State mentioned that EIAs would be requested to be done if there is going to be impact on the environment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, can I confirm, one, whether it is an environmental impact assessment or an environmental impact study that would be requested?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, to follow up on Member Ms Nadia Samdin's point, for open-cage farming, can I confirm as well that SFA will always require an EIA to be done?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In the National Parks Board (NParks)'s methodology, they will also advise on some findings regarding marine ecological profiling exercise when assessing whether a site is suitable to be used for aquaculture activities.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is a series of tools that we use to size up the potential impact before we decide whether a site is suitable for aquaculture activity.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But even as a site is selected for aquaculture activity, there will be environmental monitoring and impact mitigation requirements on the operator to make sure that even when the farm is established, there will be ongoing measures to make sure that the impact on the environment is mitigated as much as possible.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Sorry, can the Member repeat the last question again, on open-cage farming?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Whether we will always require an EIA done when it is open-cage farming.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As I said, I think it is in relation to the main reply.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think in more advanced aquaculture countries – for example, on a recent study trip that we had undertaken with our stakeholders to Australia, we did come across this framework which the Australians used to manage aquaculture sector growth in Australia, to also help manage environmental impact.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is an approach to make sure that while we want to ensure the process is not overly onerous, a suitable and comprehensive one is done for the overall site; yet, at the same time, post-implementation, there is a series of monitoring to make sure that the ongoing activities are also sustainable for the environment.
